title: bin/devbin gate rust --help runs the real gate: Intent's cut/gate reads only its first argument, so a trailing --help starts a heavy build with no Desk slot
body:
**`bin/devbin gate rust --help` RUNS THE REAL GATE.** On 2026-11-17 at about 10:41Z, cc ran it expecting usage, and it started the whole Rust gate at HEAD: a cold build into `cargo test --workspace`, with no Desk slot. cc stopped it after about two minutes and cleaned up by hand. Nothing in the canon tree or the live store was touched, but an unbooked heavy run is exactly what hv decision 45 forbids beside a kovacs run.

**The mechanism.** Intent's row for the gate is `gate: rust: run: bin/.devbin/cmd/measured --exec bin/.devbin/cut/gate rust` (`bin/.devbin/config.yaml:430`). devbin's `run_builtin_gate` answers `-h` and `--help` only in the option's place (`bin/.devbin/lib/gatecmd:47`), so `gate --help` prints usage, while a `--help` after the option goes on to the project's run line. Intent's `bin/.devbin/cut/gate` dispatches on its first argument alone (`case "$CHECK"`) and never reads the rest, so the trailing `--help` is ignored and the gate runs.

**The fix.** `cut/gate` refuses any argument after the check's name, naming it, and answers `-h` and `--help` with its usage, so no stray word reaches a run. Owner: dc. It rides the release hv decision 58 calls for. devbin-vc is told that devbin's dispatcher hands a trailing `--help` to a project's run line; whether devbin answers it there is devbin's call.
